Convex families are exactly interval-closed subsets; the empty family is included. For any finite order-automorphism group, fixed convex families pull back from the orbit-poset quotient; the proof aligns representatives to lift each quotient interval and grading/finite action gives antisymmetry. Burnside on the eight signed-coordinate permutations yields fixed counts 3938 (identity), 526 (two coordinate/valuation transpositions), 186 (three double transpositions), and 26 (two 4-cycles): (3938+2*526+3*186+2*26)/8=700. Orbit size profile (26,54,289,331), weighted sum 3938, and S4 count 349 follow exhaustive enumeration of exactly all 65536 potential sixteen-bit families. An independently written finite iterator recomputed 3938 convex families, D8 orbit count and profile, and S4 orbit count. The standalone check_orbits.py and check_antichains.py files were traced at frozen tree; finite exhaustion is the entire n=2 theorem, not evidence for arbitrary numbers of atoms.
